cim: Sowela launches new program for careers in analytics, artificial intelligence
cim_eredeti: Sowela launches new program for careers in analytics, artificial intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
Published 3:37 pm Monday, November 23, 2026

Sowela Technical Community College recently launched a new program that aims to prepare students for careers in data science, analytics, and Artificial Intelligence.

The new Associate of Applied Science degree program helps students develop skills in programming, data analysis, and machine learning that can lead to careers that include data analyst, junior data scientist, and AI specialist.

Student Brandi Schultz, who is also the institutional research and assessment specialist at Sowela, said the program is helping her hone the skills she needs to grow into a leadership role within her field.

“Currently, our department reports data such as enrollment, retention, graduation rates, and such. Ideally, I’d like to build on that experience by using data science and analytics to better understand the information behind those numbers and help institutions make decisions that better support students,” Schultz said.

Deciphering the information behind the analytics is what Schultz said intrigues her the most about her career field. Through the course at Sowela she said she is already growing more confident in her skills.

“My favorite part of data analytics is finding the story in the numbers,” she said. “What interests me most about AI is how it can help us come up with follow-up questions and test different ways to explore them. We can then check what we find against the data and use what we know about our students and institution to make sense of it.”

Schultz’s experience reflects what Sowela leaders imagined when they chose to build the program.

“Businesses and industry are making use of significantly more data than ever before while rapidly increasing their adoption of artificial intelligence,” Sowela information systems instructor, Dr. Steven Dabelow said. “They need people who can analyze data, drive better decisions, and apply AI tools safely and ethically. Preparing students with those capabilities is how Sowela is responding to the changing workforce demand.”

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projects that data scientist employment will become one of the fastest-growing career fields by the mid-2030s. Sowela’s advisory committee, which consists of local industry partners, has confirmed the demand for the program and helped shape the curriculum currently being offered.
